stories.title: Alleged gunman at White House Correspondents' Dinner appeared in court
stories.summary: The alleged gunman at the White House Correspondents' Dinner appeared in court Monday  for his arraignment, where he faced charges of attempted assassination of the president, among others.

stories.title: This week in space news: Artemis II next steps and a mysterious interstellar visitor
stories.summary: NPR's Scott Detrow talks with Regina Barber and Nell Greenfieldboyce about the Artemis moon missions, the "seismic quiet" during a solar eclipse, and the origins of a mysterious interstellar visitor.

stories.title: Why the Stillaguamish Tribe in Washington is buying up farmland
stories.summary: The Stillaguamish Tribe north of Seattle is returning farmland to the sea to save salmon and help floodproof a community that's struggled with rising tides due to climate change.

stories.title: A driver lifted a teen's spirits at a stoplight
stories.summary: Forty years ago, a 19-year-old woman sat behind the wheel of her car, sobbing and feeling like her life had fallen apart. A stranger pulled up beside her at a stoplight and lifted her spirits.

stories.title: Internet blackout causes huge damage to Iran economy
stories.summary: Iran has cut off the internet during the war, and the blackout is hurting businesses and the crumbling economy.

stories.title: Prison guards and inmates say New York's correctional system is broken
stories.summary: Prison guards in New York say the state's correctional system is in crisis. Both guards and inmates are pleading with the state to fix what they say is a broken system.
